articleTitle: Abstract of the address entitled ‘the international geophysical year 1957–58’
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper began by reminding those present of the work of the Institute's first Lightning Investigation Committee under the direction of Dr B. F. J. Schonland, F.R.S., which was the fulfilment of a policy originated by Dr Bernard Price when he was President. This policy committed the Institute to supporting a piece of basic physical research in an electrical field, and the work of the Committee, and what followed from it, indicated clearly the need for close cooperation between the electrical engineer and the pure physicist in problems in such a field. Each has a definite and distinct contribution to make before a satisfactory solution can be found, and both are needed for this solution. Following this policy the local Committee had asked a physicist to give the inaugural paper on basic researches at present in progress.

articleTitle: A note on rhe design of transductors for maximum power transfer
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The optimum conditions for maximum power transfer are described and relatively straightforward formulae developed for designing a transductor to get maximum power output for the smallest physical size of the as yet relatively expensive core material. It is shown that for most applications solution of the matching problem given by conventional circuit analysis does not hold.

articleTitle: Some comments on regulations and other problems appertaining to electrical installations in South Africa
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Note. This paper is to be read in conjunction with the second edition as amended in August, 1955, of the Standard Regulations for the Wiring of Premises issued by the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers. The paper lists some of the causes of the present very unsatisfactory regulations governing electrical installations. It then examines these causes in more detail, giving examples from the Standard Wiring Regulations of unsatisfactory regulations with recommended alternatives. Finally, recommendations are made for the improvement of the position.

articleTitle: Low resistance earth electrodes—their achievement and accurate measurement
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The electrical characteristics of various soils and the effects of moisture content, temperature, added salt and coke are first discussed. The effect of the shape of an earth electrode is then examined as well as the necessity of spacing parallel connected earth electrodes far enough apart to avoid overlapping of their resistance zones. Finally the various methods of measuring earth electrode resistances are investigated and their accuracy tested.

articleTitle: The protection of low-voltage installations by means of miniature circuit breakers and H.R.C. Fuses
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: An analysis of discrimination tests between miniature circuit-breakers and h.r.c. fuses, of short-circuit calculations for typical cases and of published fuse characteristics leads to design rules for the protection of low-voltage installations. The use of h.r.c. fuses on main-distribution boards and of miniature circuit-breakers on sub-distribution boards appears functional, subject to careful discrimination design. Based on the hypothesis that discrimination is determined by the 0.01 -sec fusing current the choice of slow or fast h.r.c. fuses is discussed. The use of various protection devices and their combinations is surveyed.

articleTitle: Protection systems against the Hazard of electric shock in mines
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The conditions under which fatal shocks can occur on the 500-volt three-phase electrical distribution networks commonly used underground in gold mines in Southern Africa are examined and the requirements for protection against the hazard are established. Basic methods of protection are listed. Safe electrical conditions for human beings and other fundamental aspects of the problem are discussed. Each method of protection is then analysed and its performance established in relation to its parameters. By comparison with the requirements it is possible to limit the choice of suitable protection systems for practical application to either the more sensitive versions of the current-operated earth-leakage protection or to earth-continuity protection, which is a new method.

articleTitle: Some comments on regulations and other problems appertaining to electrical installations in South Africa
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Mr C. G. Downie's report on the basis of my paper is very much appreciated. He does not agree with my suggestion that a national organisation be constituted to control inspectors, but admits that to obtain a high degree of uniformity of interpretation in his own supply area, frequent meetings of inspectors are held to discuss the interpretation of regulations. Would not the extension of this principle to a national body result in greater uniformity of interpretation on a national scale? It is also noted that certain of the present regulations notably that dealing with earthing are not acceptable to Mr Downie.

articleTitle: Crosstalk measurements between antennae on the Johannesburg—Pretoria micro-wave radio system
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper deals with measurements made on the Pretoria-Johannesburg microwave radio system in order to establish the crosstalk margins at repeater stations between signals in the two directions of transmission of the system. The investigation was necessitated by the occurrence of what appeared to be excessive and variable noise-levels on the speech channels provided by the system. The methods of measurement, the measures taken to increase the crosstalk margin and the conclusions in regard to siting of repeater stations of this type are given.

articleTitle: Design and operating experience with large turbo-type A.C. generators
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Summary The paper deals with some of the problems encountered in the design of the larger turbo-type a.c. generators which were built during the last 15 years, and those under construction at present. The main problem is to produce reliable, efficient machines with long life and requiring the minimum maintenance, at an economic price, and of weight and dimensions which are within the available transport limits. In many cases the latter item presents the greatest difficulty because it conflicts with the other main requirements. It is regretted that in many countries transport facilities have not kept pace with the demands of the times. Basically a turbo-generator consists of a stator, with its frame, core, and insulated windings, a solid steel rotor with its insulated windings and means for removing the heat losses from these parts. Most of the new problems encountered have been concerned with conditions which have arisen due to the increased capacity of units and the introduction of hydrogen cooling.

articleTitle: Airborne geophysical prospecting
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: It was a great and unexpected honour to me to be invited to give this memorial lecture tonight in honour of Dr Bernard Price. One of the reasons for this invitation was, I understand, that I had some acquaintance with Dr Price in the years toward the end of his life. It would be true to say that I owe to his wisdom and generosity in founding the Bernard Price Institute of Geophysical Research a large fraction of my academic life and I found that his continued interest in the work going on at that Institute made it always a pleasure to describe what we were doing, or what we proposed to do, in the prosecution of our researches.

articleTitle: The unbalanced symmetrical parallel-T network, taking account of condenser loss
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The polar plot of the transmission factor of an unbalanced symmetrical parallel-T network taking account of the loss of the condensers of the network is presented and it is shown that this type of network having a continuously variable rejection frequency is not the simple device previous authors have supposed. It is also indicated that this more complex analysis is essential when the parallel-T is used in conjunction with feedback amplifiers especially at low frequencies. The application of the parallel-T to wave-analyser and to oscillator action is investigated in the light of this more complex analysis. Experimental verification of all theory is provided.

articleTitle: Super-tension cable development
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Summary The limitations of the solid-type oil-impregnated paper-insulated cable for the transmission of super-tension voltages is discussed and the pattern of development of the various designs of special cable which are available is described. These designs fall into two main groups. The first group contains those designs which use a fully-impregnated dielectric and the second group those which contain gas under pressure in the dielectric. The merits of the alternative systems are discussed in relation to existing type testing specifications and to future developments for cable materials. The conclusion reached is that the fully-impregnated dielectric offers the greatest potentialities for the future development. The pipe-line compression cable and the flat oil-filled pressure cable systems are described briefly, reference also being made to the design modifications which are possible with the two systems.

articleTitle: Radio observations on the first Russian artificial earth satellite
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Doppler measurements made in Johannesburg, South Africa, on the first Russian earth satellite are described. The orbit of the satellite is derived from these measurements using an approximate method of calculation in which ionospheric effects are neglected and an eccentric circular orbit is assumed.
